title: FCC Amateur Extra Class (Element 4)
releaseBlockers: Part 97 text on govinfo predates the 13 February 2026 60 m change: check every rules card against FR 2026-00587
description: FCC Extra: every idea explained before it is tested, every card quoting the source words it rests on.
sourceShort: the NCVEC question pool and 47 CFR Part 97
notice: Questions marked "Pool" are from the 2024–2028 Amateur Extra Class (Element 4) question pool, released into the public domain by the NCVEC Question Pool Committee. The deck also uses 47 CFR Parts 1 and 97, Federal Register rule documents, US Navy NEETS training modules and NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center pages, which are US Government works. This deck is independent and is not affiliated with, sponsored, endorsed or approved by the FCC, the NCVEC or any Volunteer Examiner Coordinator.

E9-1.alt: Figure E9-1: a free-space polar radiation pattern. Bearings are marked every 30 degrees, 0 on the right to 180 on the left, with −30 to −150 below; rings are marked −3, −6, −12 and −24 dB from the outside in. One large main lobe points to 0 degrees; a small rear lobe points towards 180 degrees and two small lobes point to the sides.
E9-1.credit: NCVEC Question Pool Committee, 2024–2028 Extra Pool, figure E9-1

E9-2.alt: Figure E9-2: a radiation pattern over real ground drawn on a half circle, 0 degrees on the right, 90 at the top and 180 on the left, with rings marked −10, −20, −30 and −40 dB. Several lobes rise from the right: the longest lies just above the horizon, three smaller lobes point at higher angles, and tiny lobes lie near the centre towards 180 degrees.
E9-2.credit: NCVEC Question Pool Committee, 2024–2028 Extra Pool, figure E9-2

E9-3.alt: Figure E9-3: a Smith chart in the horizontal orientation. One straight horizontal line crosses the centre, marked 0 at the left, then 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0 and 20, with the infinity sign at the right. Circles of constant resistance all touch the right-hand end; arcs marked 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 and 5.0 curve from that point to the large outer circle, above and below the line.
E9-3.credit: NCVEC Question Pool Committee, 2024–2028 Extra Pool, figure E9-3 (as rotated by the errata of 31 January 2024)

E6-3.alt: Figure E6-3: six logic-gate symbols numbered 1 to 6. 1: two inputs, a flat back and a rounded front. 2: the same shape with a small circle on the output. 3: two inputs, a curved back and a pointed front. 4: the same shape as 3 with a small circle on the output. 5: a single-input triangle with a small circle on the output. 6: two inputs, a curved back and a large triangular front with no circle.
E6-3.credit: NCVEC Question Pool Committee, 2024–2028 Extra Pool, figure E6-3

E7-1.alt: Figure E7-1: a transistor amplifier. The input passes through capacitor C1 to the transistor’s base. Resistor R1 runs from the base to the positive supply and R2 from the base to ground. A resistor from the positive supply feeds the collector, and capacitor C2 couples the collector to the output. Resistor R3 runs from the emitter to ground, with capacitor C3 also from the emitter to ground.
E7-1.credit: NCVEC Question Pool Committee, 2024–2028 Extra Pool, figure E7-1

E7-2.alt: Figure E7-2: a regulator circuit. A +25 V input feeds the collector of transistor Q1 and, through resistor R1, a junction holding Q1’s base, capacitor C2 (4000) to ground and Zener diode D1 to ground. C1 (4000) sits across the input to ground. Q1’s emitter gives the +12 V output, with C3 (0.01) and load resistor R2 to ground.
E7-2.credit: NCVEC Question Pool Committee, 2024–2028 Extra Pool, figure E7-2

E7-3.alt: Figure E7-3: an op-amp circuit. The input passes through resistor R1 to the op-amp’s inverting (−) input. Feedback resistor RF runs from the output back to that same input. The non-inverting (+) input is grounded, and the output is taken between the op-amp output and ground.
E7-3.credit: NCVEC Question Pool Committee, 2024–2028 Extra Pool, figure E7-3

checks.what: Four independent audits read all 1442 cards: the 599 pool questions (checked word for word against the NCVEC 2024–2028 pool by the card checker) for the explanations of every answer and wrong option, and every other card against 47 CFR Part 97, the FCC and Federal Register documents and the Navy NEETS modules it quotes; every calculation was reworked by hand
checks.result: 6 wrong explanations were fixed and rechecked (among them a wrong-option note off by a factor of ten and one that misnamed which errata changed a citation); 17 explanations that only restated the key were re-sourced to FCC, NASA, NTIA and Navy texts; 3 unsupported claims, 6 ambiguous cards, 70 unclear ones and 85 minor issues were also fixed. Pool references made out of date by the February 2026 rule changes are flagged in their explanations.
